hints.title: Think partition, not merge
hints.body: Merging both arrays costs `O(m + n)`. Instead, split each array into a left part and a right part so that the two left parts together hold exactly the lower half of all values.

hints.title: Balance the halves
hints.body: If the total length is `T`, the left side should contain `ceil(T / 2)` values. Choosing the split in the smaller array fixes the split in the larger array.

hints.title: Check four boundaries
hints.body: A split is valid when the largest left value on each side is at most the smallest right value on the other side. If it is not, move the split in the correct direction.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
if nums1 is longer than nums2: swap them
m = length(nums1), n = length(nums2)
half = (m + n + 1) / 2
try every split i in nums1 from 0 to m:
    j = half - i
    left1 = nums1[i - 1] or -infinity
    right1 = nums1[i] or +infinity
    left2 = nums2[j - 1] or -infinity
    right2 = nums2[j] or +infinity
    if left1 <= right2 and left2 <= right1:
        if total is odd: return max(left1, left2)
        else: return (max(left1, left2) + min(right1, right2)) / 2
    if left1 > right2: move i left
    else: move i right
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete solution.
